# RESULTS

*Generated by `scripts/make_results.py` on 2026-11-21. Do not edit by hand.*

All numbers below come from the code in this repository. Model: Earth-Moon circular restricted three-body problem (CR3BP), point-mass primaries, rotating frame.

Stability index used throughout (matches the JPL catalog, checked in `tests/test_stability.py`): ν = ½(|λ_max| + 1/|λ_max|), λ_max the monodromy eigenvalue of largest modulus.

## 2-3. Lyapunov and halo families vs. the JPL catalog

Two comparisons for each family. **Interpolated:** the catalog's period and stability index are spline-interpolated at each computed orbit's Jacobi constant, within runs of the family where C is monotone. **Pointwise:** at 60 catalog orbits spread along the family, our orbit is corrected with one initial-condition coordinate fixed to the catalog value (no interpolation; valid at folds in C).

**Pointwise, all families: 360 catalog orbits, period within 3.7e-12 (relative), Jacobi constant within 2.1e-12, stability index within 9.5e-4 (relative), no failed corrections.**

Interpolated, all families: 1359 comparisons; the median period error of every family is ≤ 6.4e-12. The large interpolated maxima occur only within ΔC = 1e-4 of a fold in C (where dT/dC is unbounded and interpolating in C is ill-conditioned); the pointwise check covers the same regions without that problem.

Where ν disagrees most (L2 Lyapunov), the five worst interpolated orbits pass 845–1259 km from the Moon's centre (inside the Moon). For the nearest catalog entries, JPL's stored initial conditions close to only 2.0e-8–2.4e-7 over one period, and JPL's tabulated ν differs by up to 1.3e-3 (relative) from ν recomputed from JPL's own initial conditions. The catalog's precision, not the solver, limits the comparison there.

## 4. The 9:2 synodic-resonant L2 southern NRHO

Target period (2/9) × 29.530589 d = 6.5624 d. The nondimensional period depends on the characteristic time, so the orbit is solved with two sets of constants. All values are CR3BP. Integration rtol = atol = 1e-13.

| Quantity | JPL constants | Folta et al. (2022) Table 2 constants |
|---|---|---|
| μ, LU, TU | 0.012150585610, 389703.26 km, 382981.29 s | 0.012150585351, 384400 km, 375190.26 s |
| Period [d] | 6.5624 | 6.5624 |
| Period [TU] | 1.480457 | 1.511199 |
| Perilune radius [km] | 2936.1 | 3249.3 |
| Perilune altitude [km] | 1199.0 | 1512.2 |
| Apolune radius [km] | 71407.2 | 71222.1 |
| Jacobi constant | 3.048871 | 3.046494 |
| Stability index ν | 1.2564 | 1.3230 |
| Closure ‖X(T)−X₀‖ | 2.0e-14 | 1.9e-14 |
| Initial state (apolune, nondim.) | [1.019698684, 0.0, -0.1804456794, 0.0, -0.0981402367, 0.0] | [1.0220282138, 0.0, -0.1821014003, 0.0, -0.1032709513, 0.0] |

Perilune altitude uses the lunar radius 1737.1 km. Changing only the characteristic quantities moves the 9:2 perilune by 313 km.

No published CR3BP apolune radius, Jacobi constant or stability index for the 9:2 NRHO was found in these sources, so those values are reported without comparison. CR3BP and ephemeris values are not expected to agree exactly.

## 5. Invariant manifolds

L1 and L2 Lyapunov orbits at C = 3.15; 300 seeds per manifold, step d = 50 km along the eigenvector (position part normalised), section x = 1 − μ, y < 0, arcs up to 35.5 d, stopped at the lunar or Earth surface.

| Orbit | Period [d] | ν | Closure |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 Lyapunov | 12.6102 | 938.9 | 1.0e-13 |
| L2 Lyapunov | 15.1622 | 594.3 | 1.0e-11 |

| Manifold | Eigenvalue | Reached section | Lunar impacts | Jacobi drift max / median | Jacobi offset from step (max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 unstable | 1877.77 | 192 | 108 | 5.0e-11 / 4.6e-12 | 8.6e-8 |
| L2 stable | 0.000841395 | 233 | 67 | 2.9e-11 / 4.3e-12 | 6.4e-8 |

The Jacobi offset introduced by the step is second order in d (the eigenvectors are tangent to the constant-C surface); the drift column is integration error.

**Step-size sensitivity.** Distance from each section point to the d = 50 km section curve (y in km, ẏ in m/s):

| d [km] | L1 unstable: Δy median / p95 [km] | Δẏ p95 [m/s] | L2 stable: Δy median / p95 [km] | Δẏ p95 [m/s] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 1.69 / 5.61 | 0.0073 | 1.16 / 2.61 | 0.0039 |
| 10 | 1.78 / 5.86 | 0.0067 | 1.10 / 2.79 | 0.0058 |
| 25 | 1.34 / 5.72 | 0.0065 | 1.31 / 2.48 | 0.0053 |
| 100 | 1.36 / 6.31 | 0.0074 | 1.40 / 2.60 | 0.0070 |
| 200 | 1.77 / 6.12 | 0.0076 | 1.19 / 2.61 | 0.0068 |
| 500 | 1.35 / 6.03 | 0.0021 | 1.13 / 2.44 | 0.0031 |

Over d = 5–500 km the section curves agree to ≤ 6.3 km (p95), the same order as the spacing of the sampled curve, so the results are insensitive to the step size in this range.

**Heteroclinic connection (L1 → L2 Lyapunov, stretch goal).** Refined over the two manifold phases so that y and ẏ match at the section:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Phases on L1 / L2 orbit (fraction of period) | 0.618496 / 0.484718 |
| Section crossing y | -19170.0 km |
| Position mismatch at section | 2.8e-9 km |
| Velocity mismatch at section | 0.013 mm/s |
| Time L1 orbit (+50 km) → section | 11.12 d |
| Time section → L2 orbit (+50 km) | 14.45 d |

The velocity mismatch comes from the two sides' slightly different Jacobi constants after the step (second-order offset, above).
